articleTitle: Prospective for nanoplasmonic active devices: Critical assessment
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The discussion will focus on compensating loss in Nanoplasmonic waveguides and assessed feasibility of developing subwavelength sources of coherent radiation (spasers). Large metal loss combined with reduction of spontaneous lifetime (Purcell effect) make these tasks exceedingly difficult.

articleTitle: Micro optics for the filtering and shaping of ultrashort optical pulses
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An axicon is known to generate a “non-diffractive” Bessel beam in the near-field or a ring illumination in the far-field. Here, we discuss the use of axicons for coupling and beam shaping, for spatial and temporal applications.

articleTitle: Recent progresses in brillouin distributed fibre sensing
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optical fibre sensors based on stimulated Brillouin scattering have now clearly demonstrated their excellent capability. While classical configurations have practically a spatial resolution limited to 1 meter, novel approaches have been demonstrated that can overcome this limit.

articleTitle: High contrast metastructures for silicon photonics
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A new class of planar optics has emerged using near-wavelength gratings with a large refractive index contrast. We will review how this seemingly simple structure lends itself to extraordinary properties, which can be designed top-down based for integrated optics on a silicon substrate.

articleTitle: Singel molecule fluorescence spectroscopy couples with cell imaging and solid state NMR to reveal the earliest events in Alzheimer's disease
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The earliest detectable transformation in Alzheimer's is the transition from monomers to oligomers of amyloid beta. We have discovered an aggregation related structural transition that seems to strongly alter the bio-acitivityof this species.

articleTitle: Designing metamaterial structures for controlling optical processes
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Resonant metamaterial structures are designed to have almost unit absorbance over selected frequencies bands. Simple metamaterial structures, optimized from both the viewpoints of performance and fabrication, can show single-band, multi-band and even controllable saturable absorption.

articleTitle: All optical clocked D flip flop using single micro-ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optically pumped single ring resonator based clocked D flip flop is reported and numerically simulated. Proposed design is simple, yet novel, and will be helpful for future all optical signal and information processing.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics integrated design
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Silicon photonics is a fast-growing technology, but the design capability for large-scale photonic-electronic circuits is lacking. Challenges include signal handling, variability and photonic-electronic co-integration. We will discuss these and the tools we are developing.

articleTitle: Energy aware free space optical access network
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In the present paper we have first compared the energy consumption in FSO access network with PONs and WOBAN access networks and later presented an energy aware algorithm for the FSO access mesh network.

articleTitle: 4×4 Optical data vortex switch fabric: Fault tolerance and terminal reliability analysis
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Reliability and fault tolerance are the important factors for multistage interconnection networks. In this paper, we propose a hardware model of 4x4 data vortex switch fabric. Also, we analyse the terminal reliability of the architecture.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of ground to satellite FSO system with DAPPM scheme in weak atmospheric turbulence
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, performance of FSO system with DAPPM (A×L = 16) scheme has been analysed. We find that, at relatively low turbulence, increasing the number of amplitude levels improves the performance of the DAPPM scheme. At relatively high turbulence, performance is improved initially and then it starts degrading.

articleTitle: Two zero dispersion points and enhanced nonlinearity in microstructured fibers: Role of core structure
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Microstructured fibers with high nonlinearity and tailored dispersion are designed, optimized and fabricated. Two zero dispersion points are achieved by varying and optimizing the core shape that can be critically controlled during fiber drawing process.

articleTitle: Optical measurement of velocity profiles in the vicinity of a Lorentz Force actuator with a high spatial resolution
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An implementation of a novel two component laser Doppler fluid velocity measurement system is realized to measure velocity profiles in front of a Lorentz Force Actuator with a high spatial resolution of 20 µm.

articleTitle: Generation of low divergent high power supercontinuum through a large mode area photonic bandgap fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report generation of broadband low divergent supercontinuum over the entire wavelength window of 1.5 to 3.5 µm from a 2.25 meter long effective single moded photonic bandgap fiber with mode area of 1100 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Power Optimised Segment Based Shared Path Protection in optical packet switched networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This paper presents sleep mode strategy to achieve minimal power consumption with Segment Based Shared Path Protection. Saved power is used for enhancing the data rate incorporating a contention resolution algorithm.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon resonance imaging biosensor based on graphene multilayer
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Using graphene on aluminum and silicon as coupling element, we propose highly sensitive surface plasmon resonance based biosensor. Sensitivity of the proposed biosensor is 400% higher than corresponding gold based sensor.

articleTitle: BER analysis of free space optical communication systems with channel state information derived from reference continuous wave light
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An optimum optical signal detection scheme is proposed for reducing the scintillation effect. A BER analysis of the signals is made using the instantaneous fading coefficient determined by a reference continuous light, shows an improvement in the performance.

articleTitle: A Long Period Grating based biosensor for the detection and estimation of cholesterol
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A Fiber Optic sensor for the detection and estimation total cholesterol has been designed and developed. The Long Period Grating (LPG) sensor developed showed a linear response in the range of 500ppm to 4000ppm of cholesterol levels. This is highly desirable for a commercial cholesterol sensor as the level of cholesterol for normal humans ranges from 1400ppm to 2000ppm.

articleTitle: Ultra-amplification of Surface Plasmon Coupled Emission using an engineered graphene-silver thin film hybrid
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the selective ultra-amplification of the Surface Plasmon Coupled Emission by synergistic plasmon coupling on incorporating a novel hybrid thin film stacking of graphene on silver.

articleTitle: Photo-induced patch antenna for frequency and beam reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A novel photo-induced mm wave patch antenna is created dynamically by optically illuminating silicon to generate a high conductivity region. By changing the illumination pattern the resonant frequency and radiation pattern can be reconfigured.

articleTitle: Polarization-doped InGaN based blue light-emitting diode with reduced efficiency droop
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: GaN/InGaN based light-emitting diode (LED) is designed exploiting the recently-discovered polarization-induced doping phenomena in III-nitride semiconductors. LED structure employing InGaN barrier, combined with the polarization-induced doped electron-blocking layer (EBL) shows promising results.

articleTitle: OFDM for frequency coded quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose OFDM to improve key generation rate of frequency-coded QKD system. Simulation results show raw keylength of 20 kbits/s for link lengths upto 50 km. Frequency guard bands and the choice of orthogonal sub-carrier spacing reduces noise power, leading to lower QBER and increased link length.

articleTitle: Polarization shift keying for free space QKD: Effect of noise on reliability of the QKD protocols
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A practical scheme for measurement-device-independent polarization shift keying using two state polarization encoding is presented. Most of the previous work on optical free space laser communications through the atmosphere was concentrated on intensity modulated systems. However, polarization modulated systems may be more appropriate for such communication links, because the polarization seems to be the most stable characteristic of a laser beam while propagating through the atmosphere. Thus, a detailed comparison between intensity and polarization modulated systems is of big interest.

articleTitle: Design and modeling of tunable mid-IR fiber laser using thulium doped fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The design details of a tunable fiber ring laser emitting in the mid-IR is presented. Thulium doped fiber is used as the gain medium, and laser is found to be tunable from 1845 nm to 1945 nm, with the appropriate choice of cavity parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of 2D photonic bandgap waveguides using a simple analytical method
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An analytical approximate method, VOPT, is applied to a two-dimensional photonic bandgap waveguide and coupler to understand guiding mechanism and obtain reflection/transmission characteristics. Results show good agreement with FDTD results.

articleTitle: Generation of THz radiation from Bow tie Photoconductive antennas based on Semi insulating Gallium Arsenide
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The generation and detection of THz radiation ranging 0.1– 2 THz using indigenously designed Semi Insulating -GaAs photoconductive bow tie antennas with ultra-short laser pulses (140 fs, 800 nm) was discussed.

articleTitle: Study of electron energies in core-shell triangular quantum wire using FD technique for lasing performance
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Electron energies and density of states in a core-shell triangular quantum wire surrounded by free space are numerically computed using finite difference technique, and intersubband transition energies are calculated for estimation of lasing performance.

articleTitle: A novel optical control plane for translucent WDM optical networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a novel optical control plane (P-OCP) that disseminates network component information to all the network nodes and evaluates routes considering signal quality. Results show that P-OCP obtains low blocking and acceptable lightpath setup-times.

articleTitle: Investigation of self pulsing in Ytterbium-doped high power fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We investigate self-pulsing phenomena in Yb-doped fiber amplifiers operated in the Master Oscillator Power Amplifier (MOPA) configuration and find that the pulsing happens due to saturable absorption in certain sections of the doped fiber.

articleTitle: Design implementation and performance comparison of ZCC code and MDW code for 10Gbps Optical CDMA system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: OCDMA is an efficient method of optical communication in which Optical codes is used at transmitter end in order to encode the data and correspondingly it is decoded at receiver's end. Every user has a specific code through which it encodes the data and thus minimizes the error rate in the system. Here a comparison between the codes ZCC and DW is done. As these codes have a correlation value of either zero or close to the ideal value. In this research, we have designed a system to incorporate both these codes separately and analyse the performance on the basis of BER and Q-factor taking a 50km of fibre and sending the data at 10Gbps. Further, the results are analysed using eye diagram and signal diagram for both the above mentioned codes and it was observed that DW code support only 16 users whereas ZCC code supports 18 users with minimum BER as . The codes where constructed using MATLAB and implemented in Optisystem 7.0.

articleTitle: Novel 3D displays using micro-optics and MEMS
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A portable projector can be built using a MEMS raaster scanner and laser light sources. Three recently developed technologies are reviewed: mixed-polarization based stereoscopic display, Gabor superlens based autostereoscopic display, and interaction using retroreflectors.

articleTitle: Solar day-lighting using optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Green lighting alternatives can substantially reduce electricity consumption. Solar day-lighting system, by transporting the concentrated sunlight through optical fibers, has been fabricated and tested and found to be 67% efficient.

articleTitle: Long-period fiber gratings and their sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Long-period gratings (LPGs) in optical fibers for sensing are discussed, especially on strain and temperature sensing. Low-cost fabrication by a low-pressure mercury-lamp exposure was described. LPGs in high-birefringence fiber had high strain sensitivity.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of lower aspect ratio sub-wavelength grating for polarization separation
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Highly efficient polarization separation requires very high aspect ratio gratings. The simplified modal method allows compromises between height and efficiency. Lower aspect ratio gratings are designed for 633nm and fabricated by e-beam lithography.

articleTitle: Development of fiber optic current sensor for electric power industry application
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A prototype fiber optic current sensor (FOCS) based on Sagnac interferometer is designed and tested for monitoring of current up to 4000 amperes for electric power industry application. Sensor is tested for nominal current one ampere as well as current up to eight hundred amperes. The output of sensor has nonlinearity of ±0.5% is presented.

articleTitle: Indigenous development of Laser Blood Flow Meter
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The novel optical and electronic design Laser Blood Flow Meter is indigenously developed to obtain biomedical parameters for pathological diagnosis. It provides large dynamic range 80µm/sec to 30mm/sec to measure blood flow in living organisms.

articleTitle: Selective suppression of the fundamental mode in a dual-mode photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The fundamental mode of a dual-mode photonic crystal fiber is suppressed selectively with the help of a long period grating. The system has been theoretically modeled and numerically computed with a finite-element solver. The suppression amount of 36dB is significant compared to reported results.

articleTitle: Optical parametric amplification in chalcogenide step index fiber over infrared region
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Infrared radiation as broad as 1000nm is simulated by nonlinear parametric amplification in step index Chalcogenide fiber of length 20cm with a single CW pump near zero-dispersion wavelength ∼ 2.94 µm of power 20 W.

articleTitle: Adjustable EDFA gain equalization filter based on a single LPG excited by flexural acoustic waves for future DWDM networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A fast adjustable EDFA gain equalization filter for DWDM system is reported. Using an LPG which is excited by means of flexural waves, the equalization with a gain flatness <0.3dB is demonstrated, inducing a power penalty <0.84dB.

articleTitle: Optical parametric node devices for energy efficient networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This talk will discuss the unique features of the optical parametric processes in highly nonlinear fibers for the node devices of the dynamic optical path network that can resolve energy issues of the future network.

articleTitle: Ultrafast dynamics of cavity polaritons in an organic semicondutor microcavity
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Strongly coupled cavity-polaritons are characterized by their anti-crossing behavior in the dispersion plot. 35-fs time period Rabi oscillations and polariton relaxation dynamics in a J-aggregate microcavity were observed using ultrafast spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Generation of clean femtosecond pulse from all-normal-dispersion mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser and it's amplification
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report generation of clean 160fs pulses from mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser in all-normal-dispersion configuration. By optimizing the output coupling 3.2 nJ of pulse energy is obtained and amplified to 7nJ without appreciable degradation of pulse quality.

articleTitle: Optical solitons supported by localized gain in the presence of two-photon absorption
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the existence of optical (dark and bright) solitons, with trivial and nontrivial phase, for nonlinear Schrödinger equation incorporating the effect of two-photo absorption and localized gain. Fractional-transform solitons are also explored for this model.

articleTitle: Fabrication of sub-micron patterned plasmonic templates by LIL for surface plasmon assisted SERS/SEF
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report fabrication of large-area patterned plasmonic templates of sub-micron periodicity by laser interference lithography (LIL), and enhanced Raman scattering and fluorescence. The enhancement has strong periodicity dependence due to resonant excitation of surface plasmons.

articleTitle: Nanophotonic structures for sensing: Exploiting photonic crystal and metamaterial concepts
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Nano-photonic device structures provide a promising technological base for reliable sensing in a variety of applications, including bio-medicine, the environment and gas detection. This presentation will review some recent progress based on photonic crystals and metamaterials concepts.

articleTitle: Almost perfect teleportation of entangled coherent states
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a scheme of teleporting a superposition of coherent states | α〉 and | - α〉 giving success rate of almost unity and to obtain an almost perfect teleportation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically induced transparency in Doppler broadened inverted Y-type systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We study the EIT of a probe field in a Doppler broadened four level inverted Y-type atomic system. Effects of various wave-vector mismatch occurring when the coupling field frequency is higher, equal or lesser than that of the probe field frequency are considered.

articleTitle: Influence of material absorption on supercontinuum generation in photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We aim to study the role of material absorption on supercontinuum generation in photonic crystal fiber. While PCFs with cores made from different glasses are well studied in previous works with various nonlinear effects, in this paper, it is planned to investigate the dynamics of nonlinear processes of supercontinuum generation in high-index fiber with material absorption to understand the physical phenomena of pulse propagation.

articleTitle: New computational approach for image recovery in digital holography
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a novel computational method for image recovery in digital holography, which does not mimic the physical hologram reconstruction process. The reconstruction of the complex object field in the hologram plane is modeled as a constrained optimization problem with a smoothness constraint on the complex object function. The illustrative simulations suggest single shot image recovery without the need of removing the dc terms and with relaxation of the minimum reference beam angle condition that is usually required for twin image separation.

articleTitle: Level repulsions in high transmittance modes in one-dimensional random lattices
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The level-spacing statistics of high transmittance modes in one-dimensional, nanophotonic random lattices is presented. Universal behavior in level repulsion and tail exponents in the optically conducting and insulating regimes is discussed.

articleTitle: Design of long-period waveguide grating based gain flattening filter for EDWA
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We design long-period grating in a trench assisted planar waveguide to obtain gain flattening filter for EDWA. Our numerical results show 18.5±1.1 dB gain in the wavelength range 1526 - 1561 nm using the designed filter.

articleTitle: Enhanced x-ray emission from bacteria
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We show that bacterial coated glass can increase x-ray emission from intense fields by 100 times. We engineer AgCl nanoparticle doped bacteria to further increase x-ray emission and show Anharmonic plasma resonance plays crucial role.

articleTitle: Modeling of deformable MEMS mirrors in modern telescopes
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Ground based modern telescopes with AO (Adaptive Optics) are at par with the space borne telescopes in providing unprecedented quality images. Recently, deformable mirrors using MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) have become a popular choice for adaptive mirrors due to various advantages. The continuous facesheet of the MEMS mirror can be modeled with the help of theory developed for thin plates [1], [2] and [3]. In this paper we discuss the modeling techniques using energy principles and variational methods [4] and [5]. For modeling and simulations we will follow the specifications of a commercially available 144 actuator continuous facesheet deformable MEMS mirror by Boston Micromachines Corporation [6]. The dynamics of this mirror is very fast and hence is neglected when compared to the rate of corrections to be applied and it is assumed that the boundaries of the mirror are simply supported. Thus our problem simplifies to that of a simply supported thin plates static under equilibrium condition. The MEMS mirror equation under the influence of point load matrix is obtained using superposition principle and Navier solution method is used for solving the deformation matrix for a given force matrix. In the case of an AO system, first the atmospheric wavefront is measured which then gives the desired shape of the mirror. Hence the deformation matrix is known and it is required to derive the force matrix, which essentially means solving the inverse problem. If the measured wavefront has noise which is normally the case, or the transformation matrix is rank deficient, the inverse problem becomes ill-posed [7] and [8].

articleTitle: Ultrafast tunable femtosecond pulse generation by chirped sum frequency mixing
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Tunable femtosecond (fs) pulses near 380 nm are generated by sum frequency mixing between chirped and the main fundamental pulse of Ti: Sapphire laser. Tunability range of 375 nm to 405 nm has been observed.

articleTitle: Interferometrically coupled two-color femtosecond optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: we report a novel and universal technique for coupling two femtosecond optical parametric oscillators that generate two signal (idler) wavelengths and can be tuned arbitrarily and independently across the range 1500–1580 nm, corresponding to a frequency separation from ∼ 10 THz down to exact degeneracy.

articleTitle: Enhancement of two photon absorption in zinc tellurite glasses via thermal poling
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The present work bring out the effect of thermal poling on optical properties of zinc tellurite glasses.The electrochemical reaction, which allow an increase in density allowing enhancement of two photon absorption in the glass.

articleTitle: Graphene oxide (GO)-semiconductor (ZnO, TiO2) nanoparticles for broadband optical limiting
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Graphene oxide-ZnO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles are synthesized for optical limiting. Micro Raman studies reveal that GO sheets are limited to 6–8 layers. UV-Vis and FTIR results demonstrated that GO with ZnO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles are successfully conjugated.

articleTitle: A simple theoretical analysis of quantum transport of 3-dimension photoelectric effect
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: I study theoretically the external photoelectric effect from quantum dots of optoelectronic nanostructure materials on the basis of a newly formulated electron dispersion law considering the the spin-orbiting constants within the framework of k.p formalism.

articleTitle: An efficient scheme for receiver-side quadrature imbalance compensation in coherent optical receivers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel hardware-efficient quadrature imbalance compensator circuit for coherent optical receivers. Numerical simulations for 16-QAM format show that it can fully compensate the quadrature imbalance over a wide range.

articleTitle: Adiabatic quantum processing in an atom-cavity-fibre network through a manifold of dark states
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Recently, we propose a scalable quantum network [Phys. Rev. A, 85 052317 (2012)], in which all quantum operations can be executed through external control lasers. This scheme has a drawback that the number of qubits are logN for a network of N nodes. We are perusing procedure which may circumvent this disadvantage.

articleTitle: Fabrication, replication and characterization of Microlens arrays for imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper we first describe the fabrication of Microlens arrays using UV lithography followed by thermal reflow method. We then describe the steps involved in replication of Microlens arrays which is a crucial step in the mass production. Finally we characterize the fabricated Microlens arrays using Digital Holography.

articleTitle: Specialty fiber gratings for sensing GAST (Gamma dose, axial strain and temperature)
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Multi-parameter sensing specialty fiber gratings are of crucial importance for nuclear industry due to their unique properties such as high radiation dose sensitivity, viability of operation up-to 1 MGy dose. We report on our unique in-situ dose measurements of Turnaround-point LPGs and their applications for strain and temperature measurements.

articleTitle: Vapor phase chelate delivery technique for fabrication of rare earth doped optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Presenting an optimized process to deliver rare-earth compounds in vapor phase for fabrication of large-core Yb-doped fibers with uniform dopant distribution and good reproducibility. Fibers exhibit good optical properties, suitable for high power laser applications.

articleTitle: Efficiency improvement of an optical parametric oscillator using top-hat transverse profile for the pump beam
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Pulsed nanosecond optical parametric oscillators, in general, are pumped by a direct laser beam having Gaussian intensity profiles in temporal and spatial domains, which limits the conversion efficiency due to energy consumption during build-up of signal and idler intensities, and back-conversion effects. Efficiency optimization in an OPO involves reducing the loss due to these effects; however, spatial distribution of amplitude across the beam limits the optimized efficiency. We show that by using a spatially uniform intensity profile for the input pump beam, one can achieve much higher optimized efficiency because of optimum conversion across the whole cross-section of the beam. Our simulation results predict a significant improvement of ∼41% in the optimized efficiency using a pump beam with top-hat transverse intensity profile.

articleTitle: Studies on the vortex of higher order topological charge, generated by plane wave interference method
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present the phasor approach to study the vortex of higher order topological charge formed at the center of lattices structure that is generated by the plane wave interference.

articleTitle: Study of self defocusing in liquids using single beam Z-scan with high repetition rate laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the behavior of nonlinear refraction property of solvent using femtosecond high repetition rate laser pulses with close aperture z scan technique. Self defocusing due to HRR pulses highly depend on viscosity and density of the systems.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear optical properties of 2,5-DCAP crystal-A combined experimental and theoretical study
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: 2,5-Dichloroanilinium picrate crystal was grown by slow evaporation solution technique and examined using UV-Vis spectroscopy, Kurtz-Perry method and theoretical first-order hyperpolarizability, electronic excitation and electrostatic potential were computed.

articleTitle: Lévy exponents at critical excitation of nanostructured random amplifying media
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We study Lévy statistics at the critical excitation of a nanophotonic, random amplifying system. We observe sub-unity exponents for weak scattering systems that are sensitive to pump fluctuations, in contrast to strong scattering systems.

articleTitle: Using Fano resonances to influence the ultrafast plasmon damping time for nonlinear plasmonics
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We explore the possibility of strongly influencing the plasmon damping time in nanostructures for efficient second harmonic generation (SHG), using the tunability of the narrow linewidth feature in the scattering cross-section of Fano resonant systems.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication and evaluation of a micro fraxicon
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A micro fraxicon was designed and fabricated using electron beam direct writing. The fraxicon was evaluated using a DBR laser and the generation of quasi Bessel type beams and ring pattern were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Long-haul optical fiber networks: 100Gbps and beyond
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We explore various technologies that enable transmission at 100Gbps and beyond over long-haul optical fiber networks. We focus on the synergistic use of advanced modulation formats, electronic signal processing, novel fibers and advanced amplification schemes.

articleTitle: Printable laser system on a film and an optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Organic waveguide laser and monochromatic optical sensor were studied. Print-like fabrication techniques can directly mount them on PET/ITO films as wavelength monitoring microsystems. Furthermore, lasers on polymeric optical fiber as bending sensor were also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Lasing from quasi-one-dimensional random lattices of multiple resonators
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We experimentally investigate lasing from quasi-one-dimensional random lattices of amplifying resonators. The transfer matrix method is used to simulate the passive system, which suggests the origin of lasing as disorder-induced photon localization.

articleTitle: Noise correlations in dual frequency VECSEL
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have experimentally and theoretically explored the degree of correlation of intensity noises of two orthogonally polarized modes in a dual frequency VECSEL for different values of coupling by changing spatial separation between the modes.

articleTitle: U-bend fiber optic sensor using 6-mercaptonicotinic acid (6-MNA) functionalized gold nanoparticles for detection of explosives RDX and TNT
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Gold nanoparticle coated U-bend fiber probe of 200 µm core diameter and bend radius 0.75 mm, functionalized with 6-mercaptonicotinic acid was used for direct detection of vapors of explosives RDX and TNT without preconcentration.

articleTitle: Ultrafast degenerate pump-probe studies of SI-GaAs and LT-GaAs
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present the measurements of excited state dynamics in LT-GaAs, SI-GaAs using picosecond pump-probe experiment at 800 nm performed in non-resonant conditions (photon energy > E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> of GaAs). The intensity dependent dynamics are also investigated.

articleTitle: Optical, structural and morphological characterization of ZnS thin films grown by RF sputtering
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Effect of thickness on transmittance, structure, photoluminescence and surface morphology of sputtered ZnS thin films are studied. Band-gap increases with decreasing thickness. GIXRD shows cubic phase. Crystallinity increases with thickness. Photoluminescence shows peak at 475nm.

articleTitle: Template assisted growth of CdSexTe1−x photonic structures
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Thin films of CdSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf> were deposited by electrodeposition for different compositions of (x). Optical properties of CdSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf> films have been studied. Optimized parameters are used to fabricate periodic photonic structures from template assisted electrochemical deposition.

articleTitle: Comparative study of EDFA/SOA hybrid amplifier for application in broadband communication
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Experimental study in terms of gain, noise figure, and polarization dependent gain (PDG) of an EDFA/SOA hybrid amplifier is presented. It is shown that the PDG characteristic of the hybrid is better, compared to that of SOA alone.

articleTitle: Topological aberration of phase singular light beams
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Topological aberrations of optical vortices introduced by a spatial light modulator are discussed. In the presence of such an aberration, a high charge vortex breaks into equal number of unit charge vortices.

articleTitle: Fourier-transform, integrated-optic spatial heterodyne (FISH) spectrometers on planar lightwave circuits
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Operational principle of an integrated-optic spectrometer based on Fourier-transform spectroscopy is described. Measurement results of the source spectrum with 1∼20-GHz resolution using silica-based planar waveguide spectrometer will be presented.

articleTitle: Semiconducting organic polymers as hole-transport layer in solid-state dye sensitized solar cells: comprehensive insights from femtosecond transient spectroscopy and device optimization
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Device optimization and ultrafast absorption spectroscopic investigations on the role of semiconducting polymer as hole-transport layer in solid-state dye sensitized solar cells suggest their dual role of dye-regeneration and light-antenna assisting in improved photoconversion-efficiencies.

articleTitle: Comparison of thermal response of LPGs written in SMF-28 and B-Ge Co doped photosensitive fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of temperature on the spectral profiles of long period gratings (LPGs) fabricated in B-Ge co doped photosensitive fiber and standard single-mode fiber is investigated. The results obtained show that the temperature sensitivity of the LPG in the photosensitive fiber is considerably high compared with the SMF-28 fiber. It has also been observed that LPGs in a B-Ge co doped fiber have opposite sign of the temperature dependence compared with those in SMF-28 fiber.

articleTitle: Growth of epitaxial garnet films for magnetostatic wave-optical mode interaction
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The films with calculated formula Lu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.1</sub>Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> were grown on (111) oriented GGG substrate with diameters 1, 2 and 3 inch by liquid phase epitaxy using Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-base flux. Different types of surface morphology on the grown films were observed. The films' surface was smooth and mirror while the film thickness was less than 13 μm and becomes rough for thickness above this value. The grown films were characterized by measuring magnetization loops and magneto-optic Faraday rotation under magnetization reversal as well as ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) at 3 GHz. All films with mirror surface demonstrate the in-plane magnetization, high Faraday rotation and narrow FMR linewidth at room temperature.

articleTitle: Development of 52W CW spectral beam combined fiber laser source
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Spectral beam combining of three 20W fiber lasers with spectral separation of 10nm using transmitting volume Bragg gratings has been demonstrated. The output power of the combined beam is 52W and absolute beam combining efficiency is ∼ 90%.

articleTitle: Characterization of erbium-doped nanoparticles in transparent glass ceramic optical fibres
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on using nanometric mass spectroscopy and molecular dynamics modelling to characterize the composition and structure of self-grown erbium-doped nanoparticles in transparent glass ceramic optical fibres fabricated by modified chemical vapour deposition without post-ceramming.

articleTitle: Detection of methane at 1650nm and carbon dioxide at 2004nm using tunable diode laser spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Recovery of the absolute absorption line shape is demonstrated for methane with a 1650nm edge-emitting laser and for carbon dioxide with a 2004nm VCSEL. The potential for direct detection and wavelength modulation spectroscopy are explored.

articleTitle: Ytterbium doped all solid Large Pitch Fiber made from powder sintering and vitrification
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on the study, the fabrication and the characterization of an all-solid Large Pitch Fiber (LPF) made from an innovative synthesis process based on a powder sintering and vitrification. This fiber is actively doped with ytterbium and presents a large core of 50µm.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of near-field fiber probe with distinctive tapered structures
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a distinctive tapered structure of near-field fiber probe to improve the propagation efficiency. By FDTD simulations, we examine the dependence of the efficiency on the tapered structure parameters.

articleTitle: Multi-coupled aluminium nanoparticles for plasmon enhanced spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optical properties of the aluminium nanoparticle in multi-coupled configurations were investigated by means of finite difference time domain (FDTD) computational method. We demonstrate the potential of the proposed structures for plasmon-enhanced spectroscopy and Raman sensing in UV region with large near-field enhancement.

articleTitle: Controlled polarization engineering by holography
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have demonstrated use of holography for controlled generation of polarized light. This permits easy generation of desired spatial polarization structure, of course under limitation of holography, in comparison to conventional polarization optics method.

articleTitle: Dynamically reconfigurable interferometric optical tweezers: Tailoring 3D colloidal lattices and tunable micromachines
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Real-time controlled manipulation of microparticles optically trapped in three dimensional (3D)-trap array lattices generated by dynamically reconfigurable phase engineered non-coplanar multiple plane wave interference in an umbrella-like beam geometry is presented. Reconfigurable stable 3D interferometric optical tweezers belonging to diverse transverse rotational symmetry are realized and used to trap micrometer sized silica beads to build colloidal lattices. Further, in addition to dynamically controlled translation of trapped array of particles, rotation of intertwined helically-stacked microparticles assemblies as real-time tunable light-driven micromachines is also presented.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic and laser properties of Sm3+ ions doped lithium fluoroborate glasses
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The present work reports the effect of concentration on photoluminescence properties of Sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions doped lithium fluoroborate (LFB) glasses by using the absorption, emission and decay measurements. The Judd-Ofelt theory has been used to evaluate the three Judd-Ofelt intensity parameters and calculated oscillator strengths. LFBSm glasses exhibit intense reddish-orange emission when excited with 405 nm wavelength. Concentration quenching has been noticed beyond 1.0 mol% of Sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ion concentration. The decay curves of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</inf> level exhibited single exponential at lower concentrations and turn to non-exponential at higher concentrations. The evaluated radiative properties suggest that the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</inf>→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/2</inf> (602 nm) transition is responsible for reddish - orange luminescence which might be used in the development of visible lasers for photonic applications.

articleTitle: Bidirectional method for multiple reflecting structures based on a nonparaxial split-step finite difference method
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a new bidirectional beam propagation method based on a nonparaxial scheme. The method can simulate nonparaxial propagation in multiple reflecting structures very efficiently. It can simulate high-index discontinuity and evanescent fields very efficiently.

articleTitle: Characterization of dual wavelength SOA based fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose an inexpensive, SOA-based, dual-wavelength tunable fiber laser. Dual-wavelength selectivity and wavelength difference (Δλ) tunability are accomplished over the C-band. Optical power and wavelength stability are measured at 0.33 dB and 0.014 nm, respectively.

articleTitle: Development of an all-optical tilt sensor employing Fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Simple, non-pendulum type all-optical tilt sensor design employing Fiber Bragg grating is proposed and demonstrated. Sensor, having good reversibility and repeatability, is capable of measuring magnitude as well as the direction of inclination from horizontal.

articleTitle: Stability of passive mode-locking of OPO with temporal walk off
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We carry out a theoretical investigation of passive mode-locking of an OPO with temporal walk off. We find stable mode-locked solutions even at high signal powers and determine the range of parameters for stable mode-locking.

articleTitle: High-power, fiber-laser-pumped, tunable picosecond source for the near-to-mid-infrared
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We demonstrate a stable (1.6%rms over 14 hours) picosecond source providing upto 3.5 W, tunable across 752–860 nm, and watt-level output in the mid-infrared, using intracavity frequency-doubling in optical-parametric-oscillator synchronously pumped by a Yb-fiber laser.

articleTitle: Tight focusing of cylindrical vector beam with high NA lens axicon
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Generation of cylindrical vector beam with high NA lens axicon system is investigated theoretically by vector diffraction theory. Results are potential useful such as peak-centered, donut, flattop focal shapes with extended focal depth may occur.

articleTitle: Micro-optics R&D activities at IRDE: An overview
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Micro-optics has immense potential to reduce the size, weight and enhance the performance of optical systems for defence applications. This paper describes some of the activities being undertaken in the area of Micro-optics at IRDE.

articleTitle: Azo dye-doped polymer films for optical limiting & Optical phase conjugation
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Nonlinear optical properties, optical limiting and Optical phase conjugation through degenerate four-wave mixing is observed in Disperse Orange-25 dye-doped in Polymethyl methacrylate - metacrylic acid (PMMA-MA) polymer films under low-power, continuous-wave laser irradiation. A maximum phase conjugate efficiency of 0.22% has been obtained for probe beam intensity at 0.11 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Phase conjugation is observed for both parallel- and orthogonally-polarized probe and pump beams. The maximum PC reflectivity is achieved when the angle between probe beam and forward pump beam is 7 degrees. The effects of dye concentration, inter beam angle between probe and forward pump beam on phase conjugation reflectivity are also studied. PC signal strength first increases and then decreases with time. PC reflectivity is also increased by increasing the intensity of the backward and forward pump beam. The predominant phase conjugation signal is attributed to the facts that reverse saturable absorption and large third order susceptibility of the dye molecules.

articleTitle: Study of surface plasmon polaritons with nonlinear focusing magnetic material
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Intensity dependent propagation characteristics and field distribution for SPP guided by an interface between metal and nonlinear magnetic material were obtained exactly. The mode characteristics relying on intensity-dependent changes in self-focused peak were studied.

articleTitle: Polarization holography with liquid crystals polymers and applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Liquid Crystals Polymers are birefringent molecules locally orientable. By recording the polarization pattern due to the overlap of differently polarized beams on LCP, space-variant retarders are realized. We present two applications polarization holography and coronagraphy.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic devices based on III-N quantum wells grown on CVD graphene
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the synthesis and optical characterization of GaN/AlGaN and InGaN/GaN quantum well structures grown on CVD graphene layers. We demonstrate a novel process allowing facile transfer of QW multilayers to other (cheap, flexible) substrates.

articleTitle: Sagnac and Mach-Zehnder interferometer based gain flattening of an EDFA
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The gain spectrum of an erbium doped fiber amplifier has been flattened over a range of 35nm with an accuracy of ±0.4 dB by using a novel all-fiber interferometric configuration.

articleTitle: Enhanced sensitivity of FBG pressure sensor using thin metal diaphragm
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: High sensitive pressure sensor based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) assembled with thin metal diaphragm is reported. The sensitivity of the pressure sensor is found to be 2.05 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> MPa<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, approximately 10,350 times higher than that measured with the bare FBG.

articleTitle: Lensed multicore fiber for interferometric optical trapping
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A lensed four core fiber has been fabricated using a fusion splicer. The interference in the far field between the cores of the singlemode probe was examined for optical trapping in one and two dimensions.

articleTitle: Over coupled long period grating with enhanced sensitivity to refractive index higher than that of cladding
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Response characteristics of over coupled long period gratings to ambient refractive index higher than that of cladding index are investigated. For the first time change in the peak attenuation ∼ 670 dB/RIU has been reported.

articleTitle: Study and development of 165 W of single transverse mode Yb-doped CW fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report study and development of 165 W of single transverse mode Yb-doped CW fiber laser at 1080 nm with a slope efficiency of 56.5% using double-end pumping of large mode area Yb-doped double-clad fiber.

articleTitle: Signature of band-edge-induced lasing observed in self-assembled photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report experimental demonstration of band-edge-induced lasing from Rhodamine B-dyed self-assembled all-solid photonic crystals. We discuss the origin of lasing as due to the enhancement of density of states and field distribution at band edge frequencies.

articleTitle: Fourier modal analysis on photonic structures with time-dependent perturbations
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Novel formulation of Fourier Modal Method (FMM) for photonic structures with time-dependent perturbation is developed. It is found that in case of time-dependent perturbation, Bloch modes in the modulation region take the form of mixed harmonic modes. The validity of the proposed FMM is examined by the analysis on the waveguide structure with non-reciprocity induced by time-dependent perturbation.

articleTitle: Reducing burst loss probability of service differentiated Optical Burst-Switched Networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This paper will extend the existing absolute quality-of-service (QoS) scheme to a service-differentiated Optical Burst-Switched Network. We will show that the burst loss probability of our service-differentiated model will decrease compared to the previous model [3].

articleTitle: Surface plasmon resonance based optical NOx gas sensor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An indigenously assembled surface plasmon resonance technique have been used for development of an efficient, fast and reversible optical NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> gas sensor operating at room temperature exploiting WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> as a sensing layer.

articleTitle: Pulsed laser ablation in Methyl Methacrylate to produce spherical gold nanoparticles and fluorescent nanodots
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on a novel technique to produce spherical gold nanoparticles together with fluorescent gold nanodots, directly into Methyl Methacrylate by laser ablation synthesis. Presence of nanoparticles and nanodots are confirmed from Transmission Electron Microscopy.

articleTitle: Failure monitoring in composite structures using embedded FBG strain sensors
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Damage progression, failure discrimination and analysis have been undertaken by embedding FBG sensor arrays as strain sensors. Average strain, strain gradient and full spectrum measurements were obtained from the FBGs for the structural health monitoring of composites.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser induced fabrication of a 1×2 splitter waveguide in BK7 glass
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on fabrication of waveguides (guidance at 1310 nm) and 1×2 splitters in BK7 glass using a variable repetition rate, 1030 nm, 270 fs laser. We write two layered splitters having separation of 20 µm.

articleTitle: Fabrication of high density waveguide structures using e-beam lithography
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Waveguides are an integral part of optical circuits. Fabrication of dense waveguides using electron-beam lithography is critical because of issues like stitching errors and proximity effect. We present a simple method to overcome these issues.

articleTitle: Hotspot monitoring in transformers using Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Transformers play an important role in power distribution. Online monitoring of temperature in transformer is envisaged for hotspot detection. In this paper, we have evaluated the performance of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) temperature sensor by suitable encasement for hotspot monitoring in transformer. The dynamic response of the FBG encased in a transformer to hotspot was studied by introducing the defects such as partial cut and weakened insulation in the secondary coil.

articleTitle: Curved optical fiber nano-tip for optical nanotweezer
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A fiber nano-tip is presented as non-plasmonic nanotweezer. The nano-tip, prepared from photosensitive single-mode fiber by chemical etching, generates non-diffracting beam which is used trapping particles of different dimensions and material at smaller laser powers.

articleTitle: Monitoring of corrosion in ACSR cable using Raman Distributed Temperature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: It is important to monitor temperature and corrosion in Aluminum Conductor Steel Reinforced (ACSR) overhead power cables. A stainless steel encased optical fiber sensor is incorporated in ACSR cable in place of steel core. Accelerated corrosion is simulated in the ACSR cable and the current induced temperature is monitored. The results demonstrate that Raman Distributed Temperature Sensor (RDTS) is a promising technique for both temperature and corrosion monitoring in ACSR cable.

articleTitle: Biosensor based on single mode Mach-Zehnder Interferometer waveguide
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the design, development and characterization of a single mode Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) waveguide based biosensor. Biomolecules such as Sucrose, HIgG are detected using this biosensor chip and the results are reported here.

articleTitle: Novel azo derivative for optical power limiting application in both CW and ultrafast regime
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The optical power limiting properties of a novel azo derivative 2- [Ethyl-(4-trifluoromethyl-Phenylazo-Phenyl)-Amino]-ethonol (E4TPA) thin-films were investigated using open aperture Z-scan technique (fs regime) and non-degenerate pump - probe set up with CW laser.

articleTitle: A study of CdS and Ag doped CdS prepared through CBD Technique
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A novel and simple CBD Technique has been utilized to synthesize CdS and Ag doped CdS nanoparticles and thin film with an average particle size of 7nm, characterized by X-RD, Absorption Spectrum, Photoluminescence spectrum, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM).

articleTitle: Fabrication of excitonic luminescent inorganic-organic hybrid nano and microcrystals
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nano/micro crystals are obtained by environmentally-friendly, easily scaled up solvothermal route and subsequent Inorganic-Organic (IO) hybrid nano/micro crystals of (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (20nm to about 7µm) are produced by intercalation of organic moiety.

articleTitle: Impairment-aware fault resilient routing in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This paper proposes two routing algorithms, namely, enhanced alternative path routing and impairment aware fault tolerant routing. Their performance is presented under different fault conditions like multiple link failures, node failures and physical layer impairments.

articleTitle: Studies on thermal effects of mobile phone radiation on DNA by thermal lens technique
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In the present study we have investigated the effect of mobile phone radiation on DNA by using thermal lens technique. Since mobile phone acting as the heat source, it is expected that trapping of heat in the aqueous solution of DNA occur and is leads to reduced thermal diffusivity of the solution. This experiment shed light towards the thermal effects of mobile phone on biological cells.

articleTitle: Multi-trench channel waveguide for large-mode-area single-mode operation
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a multi-layer channel waveguide design that supports a single-guided mode with large-mode area. Geometrically shaped waveguide with suitable design parameters ensure effective single-mode operation with mode area as large as 100 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Polarization based refractive index sensor in ridge waveguides
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a sensor scheme utilizing modes with orthogonal polarization states in ridge-waveguide geometry by employing a pair of LPGs. Simulations show very high sensitivity ∼ 5200 nm/ARI over (1.33–1.34) RI range in S+C band.

articleTitle: Laser induced gold nanoparticle egg-white protein conjugation and thermal denaturation
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Spectroscopic study of laser induced one-step conjugation of gold nanoparticles to egg-white protein shows shift in amide I β-sheet structure of protein and thermal denaturation of proteins due to localized heating of gold nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance based optical fiber humidity sensor with etched fiber core comprising enhanced sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance based optical fiber humidity sensor is developed by chemically synthesizing gold nanoparticle film onto the etched core region of a multimode optical fiber. Linear response is observed with greatly enhanced sensitivity.

articleTitle: Rare earth doped fibers for fiber laser: Opportunities and challenges
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The advancement in the design and fabrication technology of rare earth doped fibers opens up exciting opportunities for realization of laser systems in a range of wavelengths with designed power levels for diverse applications.

articleTitle: Detection of cold dilute gases with cavities
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Cold dilute gas mixtures with small numbers of atoms, ions and molecules are created in specially designed experiments. Detection of the various species, using high finesse optical cavities is explored and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Spatial and spectral distribution of emission in photonic band gap structures
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The spontaneous emission characteristics of a dye-doped photonic crystal are studied over a large angular and spectral range to understand the anisotropic propagation of emitted light due to the pseudo-gap properties of the crystalline structure.

articleTitle: Synthesis and optical characterization of photorefractive inverse opal structures
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: High quality inverse opal structures are synthesized from the photorefractive SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> medium by a simple two step infiltration and calcination process. Optical characterization reveals the high index contrast and applications of them in the field of sensors and integrated optics.

articleTitle: Continuous wave 2D Terahertz imaging system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A Terahertz imaging system operating over a wide frequency range (0.1 THz–2THz) is developed based on continuous wave photo-mixing technique using components operating at 1550nm to demonstrate 2D non-intrusive imaging of a package.

articleTitle: Pulse Splitting in Coaxial Fibers due to two mode interference
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A Gaussian temporal light pulse propagating through a coaxial fiber splits into a series of narrow pulses due to interference between the two excited modes which have equal group velocity and opposite group velocity dispersion.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery modes of microcavities for sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)

authors.preferredName: CH. S. R. V. S. Raju

abstract: Whispering gallery modes (WGMs) of microcavities are extremely sensitive to their size and the refractive index. WGMs of micrometer-sized spheres and cylindrical fibers are used for sensing applications by comparing with theoretical simulations.

articleTitle: Quantum tunneling effects on optical soliton switching in an erbium doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We discuss the effect of nonlinear tunneling in optical soliton switching in an erbium doped fiber which is described by Generalized Inhomogeneous Nonlinear Schrödinger Maxwell-Bloch (GINLS-MB) equation. To analyze this concept two soliton solution is derived via Darboux Transformation associated with Lax pair. In this paper, we investigate that what is the role of tunneling effect on soliton switching mechanism. Our result reveals that Soliton tunneling may create a new field of applications of optical solitons as the tunneling effect makes it possible to design new kinds of all-optical switches and logic circuits.

articleTitle: Novel Fabry-Perot resonant plasmonic crystals for nanophotonic applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Plasmon mediated enhancement in the local field has wide practical applications. Here we report novel structures, suitable for trapping applications, which support Fabry-Perot plasmonic modes in the horizontal cavity formed inside the slits.

articleTitle: CN, C2 molecular emissions from pyrazole studied using femtosecond LIBS
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We investigated the decay of elemental (C, H, N, O) and molecular spectral features (CN and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) in Pyrazole using femtosecond LIBS. Temporal features of CN/ C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CN/C C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/C, CN/N and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/N ratios are studied.

articleTitle: Optical notch filters with precise production control using regenerated Fiber Bragg Gratings
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A new way to produce a controlled notch filters based on regenerated Bragg grating is demonstrated. This can be used in several photonics applications, such as RF-filtering or subcarrier processing, where specific notch filters are required.

articleTitle: Semiconductor laser dynamics with two filtered optical feedbacks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We study eperimentally and numerically the dynamics of a semiconductor laser subject to FOFs from two separate external cavities. Our results show that the inclusion of second FOF introduces rich control over the laser frequency.

articleTitle: Hyper-entangled photon pairs using integrated optical waveguide device
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a scheme for the generation of hyper-entangled photon pairs using an integrated optical waveguide device; the biphoton output state is simultaneously entangled in polarization and spatial modal degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Dark and bright optical solitons in Non-linear Schrödinger equation: The decomposition method
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper we have introduced an elegant approximation scheme called the decomposition method for solving the Non-linear Schrödinger type of equations. We show that, the methodology provides a systematic way to find bright and dark soliton solutions of the NLS equation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear enhancement in 1-D photonic crystal with ZnO defect fabricated by rf sputtering
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Large enhancement in nonlinear absorption (NLA) was observed in 1-D photonic crystal containing ZnO defect fabricated by rf sputtering. The enhancement in NLA is due to the strong confinement of the optical field around the defect layer.

articleTitle: Effect of phase modulated on tightly focused radially and azimuthally polarized double ring shaped beam
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a new approach for generating multiple focal spots and focal holes segment of sub wavelength size, by tight focusing of phase modulated double ring shaped radially and azimuthally polarized beam respectively using vector diffraction theory.

articleTitle: Microwave controlled Electromagnetically Induced Transparency inside an RF cavity
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We detail the construction of a microwave cavity resonator at 3.0357 GHz. We describe the effect of this resonator on the Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) phenomenon shown by <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</sup>Rb: atoms enclosed within the resonator.

articleTitle: The role of the asymmetry of a dispersion map in a high speed dispersion managed optical communication system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The numerical investigation of the role of the asymmetry of a dispersion map in a high-bit-rate DM system, which has predicted a significant improvement in the intrapulse collision distance, if asymmetric dispersion map is used.

articleTitle: A novel low-cost bidirectional multimedia data transmission using optical fiber in RoF system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Full-duplex multimedia signal over single mode fiber using wavelength-division-multiplexing and Mach-Zehnder-Modulator is proposed and demonstrated. Our proposed scheme is suitable for100 km SMF transmission with excellent BER and eye-opening.

articleTitle: Chalcogenide glass as a nonlinear dielectric in a nonlinear metamaterial structure
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We theoretically investigate using of Chalcogenide glasses in a metamaterial structure and obtain an intensity dependent magnetic permeability. We also numerically investigate the role of the dielectric used in a fishnet metamaterial structure at microwave wavelengths.

articleTitle: State-of-the-art in cw photomixing systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Frequency-domain terahertz techniques offer spectral selectivity, high resolution and excellent signal-to-noise ratios. Two-color distributed feedback (DFB) diode lasers now form the basis of compact and portable systems. Photomixers - photoconductors or fast p-i-n photodiodes - convert the optical beat signal of the two lasers into tunable, narrow-band terahertz radiation. Optimized laser tuning and data processing algorithms reduce the acquisition time for a complete spectrum from several hours to below 2 minutes. This talk compares THz systems based on GaAs photomixer technology and recent developments using InGaAs/InP emitters and detectors. Selected application examples are presented.

articleTitle: Generation of terahertz radiationin ZnGeP2 by difference frequency mixing technique using femto seconds laser system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Theoretical approach is developed to evaluate ZnGeP2crystal for the generation of THz radiation by DFM using Ti:Sapphire femto second laser. We have ascertained the phase-matching angle, GVM, GVD and length of crystal.

articleTitle: Low-loss erbium activated silica-tin oxide planar waveguides
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
