abstract: New classes of erbium-doped silica-based planar waveguides are fabricated by the uniform deposition of photorefractive, low-phonon energy SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with 25% maximum molar composition. The optical properties reveal low attenuation coefficient of 0.5±0.2 dB/cm at 1.54µm.

articleTitle: Ultrashort dark soliton pulse evolution in the variable-coefficient modified nonlinear Schrödinger model
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, the variable-coefficient modified nonlinear Schrödinger model investigated, which describes the ultrashort dark one-soliton pulse evolution and propagation dynamics with the distributed dispersion, self-phase modulation, self-steepening and linear gain/loss. The dark one-soliton solution is obtained with Hirota's bilinear method.

articleTitle: Narrowband optical parametric amplification in slow-light engineered GaInP photonic crystal waveguide
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optical parametric amplification by four-wave mixing in engineered GaInP photonic crystal waveguides is accurately derived with the inclusion of dispersive nonlinearity and losses. Narrowband optical parametric amplifications are achieved for tunable slow light device application.

articleTitle: Photonic applications of carbon nanotube and graphene
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We review photonic and optoelectronic applications of carbon nanotube (CNT) and graphene to such as light emitting, nonlinear, photovoltaic, modulating, and transparently conducting devices. We also present our works on application to short-pulse fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Photonics in the pursuit of living cell membrane structure
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The cell membrane is a fluid bilayer, composed of a number of proteins and lipid species. Here I discuss how a variety of photonic tools have been used in the pursuit of understanding the dynamic architecture of the living cell membrane at the nano and meso scale.

articleTitle: All optical integrator based on FBGs and Fabry-Perot Fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report all optical Integrator based on FBGs and FP_FBGs which has been analyzed to determine the impulse response for various impulse pulse excitations.

articleTitle: Effect of surface interactions on diffusion of molecules: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopic investigation
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy study showed that apart from its surface charge, the hydrophobicity of the substrate significantly influences the diffusion of the molecules and must be taken into account for a correct interpretation of the FCS data.

articleTitle: Designing high-performance fiber laser with triangular-lattice photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Designing a high-performance fiber laser with triangular-lattice PCF is reported. Using finite-difference mode-calculation algorithm devised with population-propagation rate-equation, we perform a series study by varying associated fiber parameters in achieving this result with reduced splice-loss.

articleTitle: Experimental investigations of random laser emission in a microfluidic channel
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have designed a promising optofluidic laser device based on a microfluidic structured channel filled with an ethanolic dye solution. We report random laser emission attributed to the inherent randomness of the structure. The systematic study of the emission dependence on various pump laser parameters reveals fundamental aspects as well as potential applications of this system.

articleTitle: Self-similar evolutions of trigonometric and Hermite-Gaussian optical pulses in asymmetric twin-core fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We analytically explore two novel types of asymptotic self-similar solutions, termed trigonometric and Hermite-Gaussian pulses of the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation with varying dispersion, nonlinearity, gain or absorption, and external source. Under certain physical conditions, we reduce the coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations to a single-wave equation that aptly describes similariton propagation through asymmetric twin-core fiber amplifiers.

articleTitle: Photofluidics — A new platform for biophotonics
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The synergistic integration of photonic and fluidic components in microfluidics, offers the possibility to create alignment-free devices with novel functionalities and enhanced sensing capability. This paper presents recently developed bespoke photofluidic devices for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of variation of THz emission angle in periodically poled lithium niobate
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this work, numerical analysis was performed to study the effect of ± 1% systematic error in grating parameters of PPLN, leading to a deviation in THz emission angle.

articleTitle: Analysis of spatially multiplexed channels to demonstrate and measure orbital angular momentum of photons in 62.5µm multimode fiber channels
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Orbital Angular Momentum in a standard 62.5μm multimode fiber is demonstrated and measured for a 4 channel spatial division multiplexed system. Experimental results show that bandwidth of optical systems can be increased 8 folds.

articleTitle: Tight focusing of amplitude modulated HyGG type — II beam using high NA lens axicon
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The focal field of high NA lens axicon with an amplitude modulated optical component is calculated by using vector diffraction theory. Numerical results show that for a radially polarized Hypergeometric-Gaussian type-II input field, the proposed system generates subwavelength focal spot size (0.386 λ) with a uniform depth of Focus (14.38 λ). We expect such a beam with small spot size and long depth of focus can be widely used in application such as data storage, biomedical imaging, laser drilling, and machining.

articleTitle: Q-switched modelocking using carbon nanotubes in an ultrafast laser inscribed ytterbium doped bismuthate glass waveguide laser
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Passive modelocking using carbon nanotubes is achieved in a linear cavity waveguide laser realized by ultrafast laser inscription in ytterbium doped bismuthate glass. The pulses observed under a Q-switched envelope have a repetition rate of 1.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Planar Metamaterial Optical Resonator
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, we report a new design of Planar Metamaterial Optical Resonator. The structure is tailored in such a way that it yields a resonator of very high reflectivity in the optical frequency regime.

articleTitle: Shaped light for biophotonics
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The use of optical beam shaping of complex light fields including Bessel and Airy modes for applications such as imaging, trapping and cell transfection will be discussed.

articleTitle: Luminescence properties of Tb3+/Sm3+ codoped oxyfluoride glasses for white LEDs
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Photoluminescence properties of oxyfluoride glasses codoped with Tb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> and Sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions have been characterized. The luminescence decay curves exhibits perfectly non-exponential nature for all doping concentration. The chromaticity coordinates and color temperature have been discussed.

articleTitle: Innovative Surface Plasmon Resonance biosensing architectures
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Surface Plasmons Resonance (SPR) architectures involving multi-wavelength interrogation are an attractive alternative for droplet biosensing. We present our results for in situ measurements of biological molecules with a two-wavelength sensor and a SPR Coupler-Disperser spectroscopic sensor.

articleTitle: Generation of vortices using cracked glass plate
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Cracked glass plate is used to generate optical vortex beam. Fork fringes in the experimental results confirm the presence of vortices in the output beam. The phase map plot of fork fringes also confirms the presence of vortices exactly at the position of forks.

articleTitle: Design of an efficient mid-wave IR fiber optic light source
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Design of a mid-wave IR broadband (3.1 – 3.8 µm) fiber-based light source exploiting FWM in a meter long suitably designed chalcogenide microstructured fiber is reported. An achievable gain more than 35 dB is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Bidirectional FWM scheme for entangled photon generation in optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a bidirectional FWM scheme to generate entangled photon pairs. Simulation shows 49% increase in signal power and 33% decrease in pump power required to obtain same conversion efficiency as in the unidirectional pumping.

articleTitle: Novel design framework for photonic integrated circuits (PICs) with active and passive sections
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Novel design framework for PICs with active-passive sections embeds semiconductor bandstructure in active sections to self-consistently evaluate the spatial profiles of each optical field and permittivity seen by it in presence of multi-fields interaction.

articleTitle: Contention resolution in optical burst switching(OBS) network: A time domain approach
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An analytical model is developed to evaluate burst loss probability in optical-burst switching(OBS) network by considering the regimes of short and long FDLs. The impact of different node non-idealities on network performance is also estimated.

articleTitle: Design optimization of low-loss waveguides and devices for THz systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The design of low loss-waveguides, simple power splitters and narrow band filters, suitable for the THz frequency band, along with the optimization of the active region of a quantum cascade laser, are presented here.

articleTitle: Final India abstracts
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the presentations and a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Final committee list
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members.

articleTitle: Agenda of sessions
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: Determining orbital angular momentum of light using simple convex lens
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We show that determination of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of an optical vortex can be possible using simple convex lens, an ubiquitous optical element found in any optics laboratory.

articleTitle: Challenges in nanoscale patterning- Interfering with interference and possible applications in semiconductor and energy sectors
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This invited paper covers the challenges in nanoscale patterning by giving an overview of the different optical concepts and approaches developed by the authors group focusing on conventional and near filed optics interference.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser-induced dot-pattern formation in BK7 glasses
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present systematic study of laser energy dose dependence on the morphology of waveguides written within BK7 glass using femtosecond laser oscillator. The guidance of smooth channels and dot-patterns is probed using 632 nm light.

articleTitle: Silver nanoparticles as radiation absorbers to reduce the effect of mobile phone radiation on DNA
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Thermal diffusivity variation in DNA when radiated using mobile phones is studied using thermal lens spectroscopy. The presence of Silver nanoparticles causes thermal diffusivity of the DNA sample to increase, pointing to a probable use as radiation absorbers.

articleTitle: Ultrafast charge transfer in silver-decorated wrinkled graphene
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Charge transfer in silver decorated graphene has been studied by ps Z-scan and laser induced transient grating techniques. Optical limiting has been observed at 1064 nm. Comparisons have been made with the dye-graphene system.

articleTitle: Transverse stress induced phase deviation measurement using sagnac loop with a distinct dual mode fiber segment
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The effect of transverse-stress applied on dual-mode optical-fiber placed in Sagnac loop is analysed theoretically and experimentally characterized. The dual-mode interference in a Sagnac-loop platform exhibits excellent potential towards configuring transverse-stress measuring all-fiber device.

articleTitle: Temperature insensitive miniature photonic crystal fiber interferometric (PCFI) strain sensors
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Ambient temperature and refractive index insensitive miniature PCFI strain sensors are fabricated using precision cleaving and fusion splicing technique. These sensors can be used to provide force feedback for surgical staplers employed in laparoscopic surgeries.

articleTitle: Dual colour cw mode-locking through soft-aperture and second order cascaded nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Stable cw mode-locked pulse train of dual wavelength with pulse duration of 9.5ps is achieved through soft aperturing of nonlinear mode in Nd:YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> gain medium caused by intra-cavity second order cascaded nonlinearity in KTP crystal.

articleTitle: Design of 2D photonic crystal waveguide based bandpass filter using electrical models of a defect
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A systematic approach for designing a narrow bandpass photonic crystal waveguide based filter by using the equivalent electrical models is proposed. An optimization approach is used to obtain the necessary defect combinations.

articleTitle: Intensity modulated fiber optic chemical sensor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Output power in fiber core depends on core-clad refractive indices. Binary liquid is used as cladding whose refractive index is changed with concentration of binary liquid. Properties can be studied by measuring output power.

Author Keywords: Change in refractive index with concentration

articleTitle: Loss compensation for surface plasmon resonances on corrugated gold gratings using an amplifying medium
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Preliminary results on compensation of the loss due to absorption for surface plasmons in corrugated gold gratings by using laser pumped Rhodamine-6G deposited on the gratings are reported.

articleTitle: An experiment to measure the Goos-Hanchen shift
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose an experiment to measure the Goos-Hanchen shift using interference. In our setup both s and p polarized beams are used simultaneously and they interfere after reflection from the sample surface, to be compared with the help of a polarizer. We also present actual results from this method.

articleTitle: Collision in phase truncation based asymmetric cryptosystem in Fresnel domain
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose collision in asymmetric cryptosystem based on phase-truncated Fresnel transform. An arbitrary image can be generated from ciphertext or watermark embedded in a host image with the help of phase retrieval algorithm. Computer simulation results support the idea of the proposed collision.

articleTitle: Optical coefficients of gold nanorod embedded tissue - Variant parameters
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this study, the electrostatic approximation is used to evaluate the optical coefficients of gold nanorod embedded tissue. These are influenced by the tissue type, size of gold nanorod and the wavelength of incident radiation.

articleTitle: Uniaxial fiber Bragg grating based accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A uniaxial accelerometer based on fiber Bragg grating is designed and experimentally demonstrated. The accelerometer exhibit a linear response with high sensitivity. The sensitivity of about 306 pm/ g is achieved for a particular cantilever mass arrangement.

articleTitle: Study on two-axis resonant fiber optic gyroscope using single source
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A resonant fiber optic gyroscope (RFOG) that senses rotation in two orthogonal directions has been proposed. It consists of a single laser source and two resonant fiber rings. Mathematical and simulations results have been presented.

articleTitle: Efficient Tm:Fiber pumped solid-state Ho:YLF 2-µm laser for remote sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An efficient 19 W, TEM00 mode, Ho:YLF laser pumped by continuous wave Tm:fiber laser has been demonstrated at the room temperature. The slope efficiency and optical-to-optical efficiency are 65% and 55%, respectively.

articleTitle: Insignificance of relative time delay between photons for a ultrafast two-photon process
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Exploring the possibility of temporally resolving dynamics in an ideal two-photon process (TPP) indicates that the existence of one-photon physical intermediate states is not a prerequisite for TPP. This study also sheds light on the phase dependence of TPP.

articleTitle: All-optical quantum switching
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We will present progress in ultrafast all-optical quantum switching. χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(3)</sup>-based devices can route entangled photons without disturbing their quantum state, whereas χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>-based devices can, in principle, lead to dissipation-free quantum-optical Fredkin gates.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared face recognition using wavelet generic Fourier descriptor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Mid-infrared face classification using wavelet generic Fourier descriptor technique has been reported. Wavelet transform applied to polar-form of face and Fourier transform has been taken of wavelet-moments. Euclidean distance has been calculated for face recognition.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis & measurement of radar signals over fiberoptic links
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This work discusses about a feasibility study conducted for various Radar waveforms over RF over Fiber links with measurement results. Also brings out experimental & theoretical results of signal delay arises in links due to fiber link length.

articleTitle: A unique behavior of pump power in the modulational instability spectra of saturable nonlinear media
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We observed the unique role of pump power (P) in the MI spectra, such that gain either increase or decreases relative to the saturation power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) and shown that operating around P = Ps is identified to be the active regime in the context of saturable nonlinear media.

articleTitle: Effect of pump depletion on transient absorption signal in metal nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Electron-lattice thermalization time in metal nanoparticles or in bulk metal are usually estimated by measuring the decay time of the change in transmission following optical excitation. Such measurements can be performed using a femtosecond laser in transient absorption geometry. We find that the decay time of the change in absorption of silver nanoplatelets in water depends on the volume fraction of silver in water for a given intensity. By estimating the volume fraction dependence of third-order nonlinearity in the same samples, we attribute the variation in the measured decay time of change in absorption to pump depletion effects.

articleTitle: Real-time three-dimensional visualization of Escherichia coli using digital holographic microscope
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this paper, results of 3-D imaging of onion peel and Escherichia coli samples are presented. The holographic data is captured by using a commercially available digital holographic microscope and the digital holograms are numerically reconstructed in real-time.

articleTitle: Fabrication of metal nano-entities using ultrafast ablation for SERS, photonics, and biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Ultrashort laser ablation of metals in liquid media was performed towards fabrication of stable colloidal nanoparticles and nanostructures on substrates. Their potential applications in the fields of SERS, Photonics, and Biomedicine are explored.

articleTitle: Super luminescent diode with a Fabry-Perot etalon for measurement of CO2 and C2H2 in a gas mixture
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Mixed gas sensing based on a broad-band super-luminescent diode (1535 nm) coupled with an external Fabry-Perot etalon for C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is proposed and demonstrated. The wavelength tuning by tilting the etalon will provide selective gas sensing by absorption spectroscopy technique.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical THz generation and applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on the development of nonlinear optical THz sources such as a high-peak-power, single-longitudinal-mode, widely tunable injection-seeded terahertz-wave parametric generator using MgO:LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> pumped by an amplified micro-chip Nd:YAG laser, which operates at room temperature.

articleTitle: Impact of dispersion profile on modulational instability in dispersion decreasing fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A theoretical study of modulational instability in the dispersion decreasing fiber is presented. A detailed discussion about the various dispersion profiles on MI spectrum is presented with proper design of tapered photonic crystal fiber.

articleTitle: Compact athermal filter in silicon waveguides for WDM and bio-sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a compact MZI on silicon platform with temperature sensitivity less than 0.2pm/K and total length around 100µm. It makes the device a promising candidate for wide range of WDM and bio-sensing applications.

articleTitle: Engineering the refractive index of lambda system using optical bistable field
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optical bistability is used to control the dispersion and absorption experienced by weak probe laser due to lambda system. We drive the system to exhibit periodic instability at lower input light strengths, and we explore nearby regime to achieve periodic refractive index and absorption.

articleTitle: Generation of sub wavelength super long dark channel using complex phase filter
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The effect of phase modulation on the intensity distribution of TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode azimuthally polarized Laguerre-Gaussian beam in the focal region of high NA lens is investigated theoretically based on the vector diffraction theory.

articleTitle: Experimental study of metal nano-particle doped optical fiber and its unique spectral property
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Silver nano-particles doped modified silica glass based optical fibers are fabricated first time by MCVD process with solution doping (SD) technique and characterized through TEM with EDX and optical absorption / fluorescence spectroscopy methods.

articleTitle: Optical clock recovery with Fabry-Perot filter based on fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Fabry-Perot filters based on fiber Bragg gratings are widely used as optical narrowband filters and as sensors. Here we propose and demonstrate all optical clock recovery (10Gbit/s, 40Gbit/s & 100Gbit/s) with Fabry-Perot filters made up of fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal modulation instability in negative refractive index materials for a single cycle pulse
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Novel regimes of spatio-temporal modulation instability for a single-cycle pulse in a negative refractive index material are predicted. The dependence of their domains of existence and properties on various parameters is analyzed.

articleTitle: Characterization of the polarimetric sensors embedded in carbon and glass reinforced composite materials for strain/temperature measurements
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The sensitivity of polarimetric sensors embedded in different types of composite materials is investigated in this paper. Polarimetric fiber sensors based on PM-Panda fiber and PM-PCF fiber are included in this comparison. The three types of composite materials used for comparison study are carbon-epoxy, E glass-epoxy, E glass-unsaturated polyester resin composite material samples. Such a comparison of sensitivity of embedded polarimetric sensors has not been previously presented and we believe that this comparison study will provide useful insights into the compatibility of polarimetric fiber sensors with different types of composite materials. The particular composite samples chosen for the study are very popular in many industrial applications and thus the work is highly relevant to smart structure applications. In addition, characterisation of the sensitivity is essential for the development of a demodulation system for such sensors.

articleTitle: Ultranarrow coherent population oscillation resonance in a Λ-type system
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the experimental observation of an ultranarrow resonance, as narrow as EIT ones, due to the transfer of coherent population oscillations to the lower states of a Λ-system.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase-reversal quasi-phase matching device for dual peak second harmonic spectral response
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a theoretical model for phase-reversal quasi-phase matching nonlinear optical device for analyzing the second harmonic spectral response. The peculiar double peak spectral nature of phase-reversal quasi-phase matching device is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Analysis of temperature sensitivity for a dual-resonant LPWG based on SU-8/NOA-61 polymers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Temperature sensitivity of a dual-resonant LPWG formed by SU-8 (core) and NOA-61 (claddings) polymers is analyzed. Temperature sensitivity for the optimized LPWG is found to be 0.13 and 0.82 nm/°C for resonant wavelength of 468 and 1550 nm respectively, which can be used for sensing and communication applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear effetcts in dye-doped polymer optical fibres for optical communication
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We review experimental studies of nonlinear optics in large-core dye doped plastic optical fibres. In particular second-order nonlinearity in all-optical poled optical fiber is promising for application to electro-optic switching, second-harmonic generation, and frequency conversion.

articleTitle: Four-wave mixing in a combination of low-dispersion fibers towards spectral broadening
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Four-wave mixing due to propagation in a combination of low-dispersion fibers is investigated using an analytical model. The first-order anti-Stokes product from the model helps in understanding the spectral broadening measured in a ring laser.

articleTitle: Design of single mode LiNbO3 photonic wires and estimation of its bending losses for different bending radii
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Single mode LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> photonic wires are designed from its fabrication parameters and bending losses are estimated for different constant curvature bent wires at 1.31 μm wavelength by effective-index based matrix method.

articleTitle: Intensity noise reduction of dual-frequency Nd:YAG lasers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Strong anti-phase intensity noise reduction is experimentally and theoretically shown for dual-frequency Nd:YAG lasers. This phenomenon is obtained by aligning the two orthogonally polarized modes along the crystallographic axes of a (100)-cut Nd:YAG crystal.

articleTitle: Squeezing the most from a gravitational wave detector network
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Laser-interferometric gravitational wave detectors are the most sensitive position meters ever operated, already pushing precision measurement to the standard quantum limit (SQL). Squeezed light may soon see its first practical application as a means to reach beyond the SQL. A growing network of kilometer-scale detectors will provide source localization on the sky, allowing detailed electromagnetic observations to follow any gravitational wave detection. Adding a proposed detector in India will greatly improve the ability of the world-wide network to localize sources and significantly increase the network's scientific output.

articleTitle: Synthesis and color tunable up-converted emission from co-doped (Er3++Yb3+):Y2CaZnO5 nanophosphor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: NIR-to-Visible up-conversion emission properties of co-doped (Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>+Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>):Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CaZnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> nanocrystalline phosphor has been studied. With increasing sensitizer (Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>) concentration, the observed color tunability (green to red) has been explored for the development of visible display devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing optical-to-terahertz conversion efficiency by using plasmonic photoconductive emitters
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We show that using plasmonic contact electrodes significantly enhances the quantum efficiency of ultrafast photoconductors and demonstrate 50-times higher optical-to-terahertz conversion efficiencies from a plasmonic photoconductive terahertz emitter in comparison with a conventional photoconductive emitter.

articleTitle: Imaging collagen and skeletal muscle fibers using Stokes-Polarimeter based Second Harmonic Generation Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We analyzed the polarization states of SHG signals through four-channel photon counting based Stokes-polarimeter. The effects of linearly and circularly polarized light are characterized on molecular structure of starch granule. Different polarization parameters such as the degree of polarization (DOP), degree of linear polarization (DOLP), degree of circular polarization (DOCP), as well as anisotropy are measured from the acquired Stokes parameters. We present a polarimetric analysis of the SHG signal emitted by collagen type I and skeletal muscle fibers, in order to extract structural information on molecular order and orientation. With the appropriate combination of input laser polarization and the detection of output polarization states of SH signal will yield the absolute molecular orientations of the samples.

articleTitle: Single mode fiber-optic temperature sensor fabricated using wet etching
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Single mode fiber-optic temperature sensor based on wet etching has been fabricated. We report a narrow, but highly temperature-sensitive etched fiber diameter region for temperature sensing applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of optical nonlinear properties of cyanine dye
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The nonlinear optical properties of PicoGreen dye were measured using Z-scan technique and measurements were carried out at different incident intensities. Both open and closed Z-scan techniques were performed and results exhibited an intensity dependent nonlinear absorption coefficient and nonlinear susceptibility at a wavelength of 532nm. These results showed that PG has potential applications in nonlinear optics.

articleTitle: Influence of Lyapunov exponent on the characteristics of chaotic optical signals from bistable acousto or electro optic systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: It has been observed that chaotic optical signals generated by bistable acousto or electro optic systems can be modeled as beta-distributed random processes. The dependence of the various properties of such signals on the Lyapunov exponent are investigated.

articleTitle: Er3+:ZBLAN waveguides for laser applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Direct written waveguides in Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:ZBLAN are analyzed with regard to laser applications. We present a simulation model for the absorption properties of the waveguides. The results from the simulation are compared with experimental results.

articleTitle: Decoy state protocol for OFDM based frequency coded quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose and analyze decoy state method for OFDM-QKD systems. Carrier ratio optimization of individual subcarriers increases key generation rate and maximum transmission distance.

articleTitle: Characterization of Optical Frequency Combs for OFDM based optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Optical Frequency Combs are becoming increasingly important for the development of future photonics systems. In this work we present the detailed characterization of optical frequency combs that can be employed in future supechannel Tbit/s transmission systems.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser micro-texturing of silicon using high repetition rate pulses for photovoltaic applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Femtosecond laser texturing of silicon was performed and three different microstructuring regimes are identified, depending on the irradiation conditions. A 70-fold reduction in sample processing time is achieved by employing high repetition rate pulses.

articleTitle: New results in biomedical image processing
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Two new techniques are described and illustrated. The first is a variation of the pyramidal algorithm. In this technique a set of filtering operations is used to enhance the image. The technique described here is simple and requires less computational power. The second describes a new pre-compensation algorithm based on the ocular point spread function. This pre-compensation algorithm based on an enhanced local Wiener filter and edge tapering was tested on 8 different types of aberrations. For this purpose, we used the Zernike polynomials to represent the 8 common varieties of ocular optical aberrations.

articleTitle: Effect of co-doping of Tm3+ ions on the emission spectrum of Dy3+ ion in tellurite glasses
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Melt quenching technique was used to prepare the tellurite glasses. Energy transfer mechanism has been discussed. Intense blue-yellow emission has been observed in the Dy-Tm co-doped tellurite glasses which is useful for solid-state lighting.

articleTitle: Continuous flow single cell electroporation in an ultrafast laser inscribed optofluidic device
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Ultrafast laser inscription has been used to fabricate a selectively etched optofluidic device incorporating a near-infrared waveguide to enable continuous flow single cell electroporation for the generation of intracellular spatio-thermal maps using quantum dot nanothermometry.

articleTitle: DFWM Measurements on Mn-(meso-tetrakis(2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-N,N,N-trimethyl-4-aniliniumyl)porphyrin) complex
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The third -order nonlinear optical studies of a Mn-Porphyrin complex using degenerate fourwave mixing has been done. Samples were prepared using standard methods. Study shows that the compound has high χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> values suitable for photonic applications.

articleTitle: Avoided-crossings in dispersion properties of photonic-crystal-surface-plasmon-waveguides
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: An analysis is presented for appreciating the mechanism of coupling of surface plasmon and bandgap guided modes. A design principle is proposed for designing such geometries and dispersion properties are studied by varying waveguide parameters.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of 3D-waveguides in Eu3+-doped oxyfluorosilicate glass
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: To our knowledge for the first time 3D-Channel waveguides have been fabricated 100 µm beneath the sample surface in an indigenously developed Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped oxyfluorosilicate glass using ultrashort laser pulses and performed the loss measurements.

articleTitle: Effect of net-fluence on waveguide formation in ultrafast laser inscribed chalcogenide glass
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Waveguides were fabricated on GeGaSEr chalcogenide glass using ultrafast laser inscription method. The thermal diffusion model is discussed for understanding the light matter interaction and shown the effect of net-fluence in waveguide formation on chalcogenide glass.

articleTitle: Microstructured optical fibers: Newest opportunity for fiber designers to realize a myriad of tailored application-specific optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Designs of a variety of application-specific Bragg type of microstructured optical fibers are reported. These include fibers for dispersion compensation, metro networks, super continuum generation, lasers at mid-IR wavelengths, and low-dispersion femtosecond pulse transmission.

articleTitle: Exact mode field solutions and dispersion characteristics of N-layered high-index-core Bragg fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report here the outcomes of our detailed studies on the propagation and dispersion characteristics of N-layered high-index-core Bragg fiber by the analytical evaluations of the mode effective indices and hence the mode-field distribution.

articleTitle: A new type of propagation in fiber: Hollow-core grating fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a new type of hollow-core fiber where the propagation is ensured by photoinduced self-patterns acting as a surface relief gratings. Such gratings act as wavelength/angle dependant reflective mirrors for propagation of light.

articleTitle: Multimode interference based temperature insensitive strain sensor using two multimode fibers in series
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A temperature insensitive strain sensor using two multimode fibers of opposite temperature sensitivities in series is proposed and demonstrated. The proposed scheme can also make various other multimode interference based fiber-optic devices temperature insensitive.

articleTitle: Depolarization characteristics of non spherical gold nano particles
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Mueller matrix measurements on non-spherical nano-particles (rods, tetra-pods, flowers and stars) reveal that rods result in highest depolarization and that the depolarization is larger for circularly polarized light compared to that for linearly polarized light.

articleTitle: Study of pulse stability enhancement in regeneratively mode-locked fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We demonstrate an order of magnitude improvement in the pulse stability of an active mode-locked fiber laser operated in the presence of natural and forced random perturbations, using a regenerative feedback scheme.

articleTitle: Decay time in a cavity in slow or negative light regime
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We investigate the decay time of a cavity containing strong dispersion achieved through electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>He*. We show that this concept is no longer relevant in the case of strong negative dispersion.

articleTitle: Polarized and un-polarized spectral characteristics of 3D polystyrene colloidal photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The spectral characteristics of (111) stop band of 3D polystyrene colloidal photonic crystals with s-, p- and un-polarized light in the reflection geometry were carried out and compared with the calculated band diagrams using plane wave expansion method.

articleTitle: A novel analytical study of different channel allocations and FWM efficiencies in optical WDM systems
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The optical WDM systems are usually affected by the Four Wave Mixing effects. This paper examines the different frequency allocations in terms of FWM efficiency for CWDM, DWDM and for three various proposed modes.

articleTitle: Investigation of nonlinear optical and all-optical switching properties of novel ruthenium complex
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The nonlinear optical, optical limiting and all-optical switching properties of novel ruthenium complex doped PMMA film were investigated at 532 nm. The investigations show that the complex is a potential molecule for photonic applications.

articleTitle: Power efficient placement of wavelength converters in WDM networks
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: This paper gives an algorithm to place the wavelength converters in WDM networks in an optimized manner to minimize the power consumption along with minimizing the packet loss probability of the network.

articleTitle: A microstructured dual-core dispersion compensating fiber design for large-mode-area and high negative dispersion
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We propose a novel dual-core optical fiber design with a microstructured inner cladding for dispersion compensation. With the present design we show − 33000 ps nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> dispersion with a mode-effective area of 68 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Determination of Mueller matrix of an optical element with Simon-Mukunda gadget
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We are describing a novel way to find the Mueller matrix of an arbitrary optical element, by taking advantage of projection of resulting polarization states on four known input polarization states by using Simon-Mukunda gadget.

articleTitle: Long period fiber grating humidity sensor with Gelatin/Cobalt chloride coating
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A long -period fiber grating coated with Cobalt chloride and Gelatin is developed and experimentally demonstrated as humidity sensor. Relative humidity variations from 35% to 90% have been detected with the sensitivity of 0.18 nm/ %RH.

articleTitle: A new codopant for rare earth doped optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Barium has been identified as a promising network-modifier, alternative to Al for rare-earth doping in optical fiber. Fabrication process has been established. Transmission and optical property of fiber indicates potential application in laser and amplifier.

articleTitle: Self assembly of large area 3D photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Three dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) are important for many applications such as photon confinement, optical switching, bio-sensing etc. Their unique property arises from the periodic arrangement of micro/submicro-meter particles. There is a lack of simple method to fabricate the same. Here we present a simple method to fabricate uniform, large area 3D PhCs using polystyrene (PS) nanospheres by self- assembly method. PS nanospheres (150–200 nm) were synthesized using styrene monomer by wet chemical method. Size tunability of PS nanospheres has been achieved by changing the cross linking agent concentration. Finally self-assembly was utilized for PhC fabrication.

articleTitle: Effects of substitutional doping on the nonlinear optical properties of single-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Using open aperture z-scan measurements in tandem with XPS measurements and Raman spectroscopy, we show that nonlinear optical properties of single-walled carbon nanotubes can be tailored by substitutional doping with Boron.

articleTitle: Spatial distribution of spontaneous parametric down-converted photons
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have studied spatial distribution of the parametric down-converted photons for a gaussian pump beam and observed that the spatial extent of these photons increases linearly with increasing size of the pump beam.

articleTitle: Metal nanoparticle induced enhancement in third-order optical nonlinearity of Phenylhydrazone/PMMA thin films
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report the third-order nonlinear optical properties of Phenylhydrazone doped PMMA thin films and the effect of noble metals (Ag &Au) on their nonlinear optical response using single beam Z-scan techniques.

articleTitle: Investigation on propagation characteristics of flat-top beam in highly nonlocal medium
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: In this article propagation characteristics of flat-top optical beam into highly non-local nonlinear medium has been investigated. A generalized exact analytical solution of the model is obtained and critical power of soliton is determined.

articleTitle: Numercial modelling of optical antenna enhanced quantum dot infra-red photodetector
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: The optical absorption of a quantum dot placed next to an optical antenna is calculated using the boundary element method and FDTD techniques. The optimized structure, shows an absorption enhancement of over 500 times.

articleTitle: Evolution of polarization singularities in few-mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Polarization singularities formed due to superposition of orthogonally polarized fundamental and higher order modes evolve as it propagates in a two-mode fiber and is used to study the vector waveguide modes and their dispersion.

articleTitle: Modeling of helium cooling tube in optical fiber drawing tower
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Convective and radiative heat transfers in annular passage between the cooling tube and moving optical fiber were investigated. Simulations show that the cooling rate increases with increase in flow rate up to an optimum value.

articleTitle: Controlled generation of in-homogeneously polarized light
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Generation of in-homogeneously polarized beams, namely radial and azimuthal polarization is demonstrated using holography and results are presented for the same. This technique can be used to generate even higher order cylindrically polarized vector beams.

articleTitle: Color image encryption using polarized light
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We present a color image encryption and decryption scheme using polarization encoding. The proposed method offers flexibility in the encryption key design. The effectiveness of the scheme is studied with numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Photon statistics of optical phase modulators and attenuators
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We show that optical phase modulation and attenuation operators do not commute in general. This has implications for frequency-coded quantum key distribution.

articleTitle: Light propagation in coupled waveguides
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We studied periodic and quasi-periodic coupled waveguides by finite difference time domain simulations. Bloch oscillations and possible light collimation observed in these structures which could be promising for light coupling applications.

articleTitle: Control of chaos in current modulated Multiple-Quantum-well Lasers with optoelectronic delay feedback
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We study the control of chaos in current modulated Multiple-Quantum-well Lasers (MQWLs), with optoelectronic delay feedback. For fixed value for delay, reverse period doubling is observed for increasing feedback strengths.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic logic gates based on photovoltaic response of bacteriorhodopsin protein thin films
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We experimentally and theoretically demonstrate optoelectronic OR, AND, NOR and NAND logic gates with multiple pulsed pump laser beams based on the photovoltaic response of bacteriorhodopsin molecules embedded in a polyvinyl matrix coated on ITO.

articleTitle: Photon correlations and entanglement: Foundational issues and some applications
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: I briefly review second order or two-photon correlations starting from the Hanbury Brown-Twiss correlations to its modern versions in quantum optics studies. With this background, I address some foundational issues in the physics of quantum correlations and quantum entanglement and argue in favour of the validity of Einstein locality, to settle a long-standing debate. Understanding entanglement from this perspective has applications in quantum information theory, especially in gaining intuition about the relation between different measures of entanglement and its time evolution. Some examples are highlighted. I discuss how ideas on photon correlations applied to squeezing fluctuations in coherent light have become important in metrology, and perhaps crucial, in the successful operation of high sensitivity gravitational wave detectors.

articleTitle: Large-pitch fibers: Pushing very large mode areas to highest powers
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: A scalable fiber design for ytterbium-doped high performance fiber lasers and amplifiers will be presented. The working principle of large-pitch fibers (LPF) bases on delocalization of higher-order transverse modes, ensuring mode-size-scalable effectively single-mode emission.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear optical properties of colloidal Cu doped ZnS nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Linear optical and enhanced nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of undoped and Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> doped ZnS nanoparticles are demonstrated. NLO properties are measured with a 10 ns pulsed laser radiation of 532 nm wavelength by z-scan techniques.

articleTitle: Tailored micro-optical and sub-wavelength structures: Manufacturing and application
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Diffractive optical elements (DOEs) are of enormous importance for applications in spectroscopic and imaging systems. We demonstrate that modified Talbot-Lithography is a fast and flexible technology for the mastering of micro-optical components, especially to manufacture high efficient spectroscopic diffractive gratings with an extended profile depth. The characteristics of DOEs also open up new opportunities for their integration in variable elastomeric optical components. We present theoretical investigations of the mechanical deformation of an initial Blazed-like diffractive grating and its impact on the optical diffraction efficiency.

articleTitle: Phase correlation study of coherent singular optical beam
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have produced optical vortex beams and measured effective phase difference between the two orthogonal field components for different polarization. Stokes vector formalism is used to quantify polarization of beam and elements of coherency matrix.

articleTitle: Studies on hardware simulation of optical interconnection Reverse Data Vortex network
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Hardware simulation study has been carried out to determine the BER performance and worst case latency of scalable Reverse Data Vortex (RDV) interconnection network with SOA based cascading switching nodes and compared with DV results.

articleTitle: Opto-neuronal interfaces and the perspective toward artificial retina
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on the new phenomenon of Cell Stimulation by Polymer Photoexcitation, as observed in primary rat brain neuron and discuss its application to artificial vision‥

articleTitle: Effect of chalcogenide glass and plasmonic metal on electric field enhancement in surface plasmon resonance sensor
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: Plasmon active metals (gold and silver) along with chalcogenide glass have been used to enhance electric field intensity by 360% thereby significantly affecting the study of biomolecular interactions occurring in the vicinity of metal-analyte interface.

articleTitle: Infrared optical fibers for sensors
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: At NRL, we are involved in the research and development of specialty infrared optical fibers, glasses, ceramics, and thin films. We have state-of-the-art facilities for making high purity chemicals and unique optical materials of high quality, which are being exploited in optical devices and systems for Navy and DoD applications. One of the core scientific areas that we have pioneered is based primarily on infrared (IR) transmitting glasses and fibers. The IR transmitting glasses are based on chalcogenide materials (S, Se, Te, and their alloys and compounds). One of our major accomplishments has been the purification of these elements and materials to levels well beyond the previous state-of-the-art. This has enabled us to reduce the absorption losses in these materials for both the mid-wave and long wave IR spectral regions. In addition to their use in bulk optics such as windows, we have developed these materials for optical fibers and their applications. The fibers and their applications can be split into two main groups, namely passive and active. In the case of passive fibers, they merely act as a light pipe, transferring infrared energy from one location to another. In the case of active fibers, they actually change the wavelength of light exiting the fiber. Some examples of both are highlighted below.

articleTitle: Study of CW and pulsed amplification in Yb-doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We have studied and amplified CW and pulsed seed signal at 1064nm in Yb-doped fiber amplifier to achieve CW output power of 6.2W and an average pulsed output power of 330mW with 33ns pulse duration.

articleTitle: Slow-light and microwave signal processing in optical circuits: Harnessing on-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 2012 International Conference on Fiber Optics and Photonics (PHOTONICS)
abstract: We report on-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering and its application to slow-light and microwave signal processing demonstrating unprecedented group-index ∼130 for SBS slow-light and narrowband (∼20MHz) microwave photonic filter with wide tunability (2–12GHz) and large Q-factor∼520.
